question: Why does the Captain Universe power leave the person who wants revenge and end up with Juggernaut instead?
core_premise: The story turns on the counterintuitive fact that the Captain Universe force does not stay with the person who wants revenge; it leaves William Nguyen and transfers to the Juggernaut, who then uses it for repair instead of retaliation.
viewer_payoff: The viewer learns that the Uni-Power abandons Nguyen's revenge plan, chooses Juggernaut, and is then used to repair the earthquake damage instead of exacting vengeance.
viewer_hook: Why does the power switch sides in the middle of Spider-Man's fight?
why_fans_ask_it: Fans care because the Captain Universe force behaves like a moral judge, not a prize: it rejects a revenge motive and moves to the character who will actually fix the disaster.
sample_answer_items: William Nguyen has the Uni-Power but wants to use it to kill Juggernaut.
Because he refuses the repair job, the Uni-Power leaves him.
The power enters Juggernaut, who then fixes the tectonic plates Juggernaut damaged during the earlier rampage.

issue_evidence.quote: Spider-Man learns that Captain Universe is a man named William Nguyen who wants revenge on Juggernaut for ruining his life during one of his rampages. When he insists on trying to kill Juggernaut instead of fixing the tectonic plates beneath New York City, the Uni-Power leaves Nguyen and enters the Juggernaut. The Juggernaut, as Captain Universe, repairs the damage to the tectonic plates that was caused by him during the same rampage that ruined Nguyen's life.

question: Why does Bucky decide to keep going after Zemo tells him he didn't earn his life?
core_premise: Zemo's taunt pushes Bucky to confront whether he deserves to live, but the concrete resolution is that he chooses survival, escapes the trap, and takes back his Captain America gear.
viewer_payoff: The viewer learns that Bucky chooses to live, escapes Zemo's trap, and reclaims the Captain America role and shield despite believing Zemo's accusation.
viewer_hook: Why does Bucky take back the shield instead of giving in?
why_fans_ask_it: Fans care because it is a blunt moral pressure point: does Bucky deserve to keep Steve Rogers's legacy, or can he claim it only by surviving and acting anyway?
sample_answer_items: Zemo frames the choice as death or facing the consequences.
Bucky accepts the ugly truth that he didn't earn his life.
Even so, he frees himself before the plane explodes and takes back his uniform and shield.

issue_evidence.quote: Zemo admits to Bucky that he would at least finish the job his father failed to do. Then again, Bucky could take the easy way out and die or free himself and deal with the consequences back home. As the plane takes off, Bucky, in the midst of trying to free himself, realizes that Zemo is right; he didn't earn his life; nonetheless, he frees himself before the plane exploded. He then reclaims his uniform and shield, as he is rescued by his friends.

question: How does the Speed Force stay under control when Barry runs?
core_premise: The Flash's power source is not just speed; it is a force that builds up excess energy and needs Barry as a release valve to stay stable.
viewer_payoff: The viewer learns the exact mechanism: Barry's running discharges built-up Speed Force energy and keeps the whole system from becoming unstable.
viewer_hook: Why is Barry called the Speed Force's release valve?
why_fans_ask_it: Fans care because it flips the usual idea of super-speed into a cosmic maintenance job: Flash isn't just using power, he's preventing the force itself from blowing up.
sample_answer_items: The Speed Force keeps building excess energy as it moves forward.
Barry taps that built-up energy when he uses his powers.
Without the Flash acting as a release valve, the Speed Force becomes volatile.

issue_evidence.quote: The speed force creates excess energy by its moving forward that builds up and needs to be released. When the Flash uses his powers, he taps into that built up energy. Without the Flash, the Speed Force becomes volatile. The Flash is effectively the Speed Force's release valve.

question: How does cosmic energy change what the Red Hulk can do?

viewer_payoff: The viewer learns that absorbing cosmic energy reactivates Ross's transformation and powers, letting him escalate from survival mode to physically overwhelming the Hulk robot.

why_fans_ask_it: Fans care because it is a strange hybrid of gamma rage and cosmic power: Red Hulk is not just stronger, he can be recharged and reconfigured by energy stolen from the machine fighting him.
sample_answer_items: Ross siphons cosmic energy out of the Hulk robot.
That energy restores his ability to transform into the Red Hulk.
Once the robot has enough cosmic energy, it becomes powerful enough to trounce the attackers until Ross later rips it apart.

issue_evidence.quote: While he faced being dishonorably discharged, Ross spent time reflecting on his life in his office. He contemplated committing suicide, but decided against it because not only was it the coward's way out, but it would be an admission that the Hulk had finally won. In the present, while the Hulk robot continues to try and crush Ross, he uses his ability to absorb cosmic energy to siphon the needed power out of the robot. This restores his ability to transform into the Red Hulk once more.

issue_evidence.quote: It immediately attacks the Red Hulk, throwing him into A-Bomb. When the two recover and fight back, the Hulk robot has absorbed the necessary cosmic energy to easily trounce the two attackers.
